newsitem.title: UK: World 1996 lead consumption at record level - ILZS.
newsitem.headline: World 1996 lead consumption at record level - ILZS.

text.p: Total world lead metal consumption rose 2.3 percent to a record 5.699 million tonnes in 1996 from 5.572 million in 1995, the International Lead and Zinc Study Group (ILZSG) said.
Total metal production fell by 1.4 percent to 5.533 million tonnes last year from 5.612 million in 1995, ILZSG estimated.
Lead mine production in 1996 rose 0.9 percent to 2.771 million tonnes from 2.745 million in 1995.
World zinc metal consumption rose 0.1 percent in 1996 to 7.535 million tonnes from 7.528 million tonnes in 1995, the International Lead and Zinc Study Group said.
World zinc metal production fell 0.2 percent to 7.317 million tonnes from 7.330 million.
World zinc mine production increased by 0.9 percent to 7.021 million tonnes last year against 6.955 million in 1995.

Western world lead consumption in 1996 rose 2.3 percent to 5.096 million tonnes from 4.980 million in 1995, according to ILZSG. Output rose 0.8 percent to 4.670 million tonnes last year from 4.635 million in 1995.
Western world zinc metal consumption in 1996 was unchanged at 6.276 million tonnes, while production fell 0.3 percent to 5.459 million tonnes from 5.474 million.
Western world zinc mine output rose 5.5 percent to 5.611 million tonnes from 5.317 million.
